text.p: Anglo-Dutch publisher Reed Elsevier remains positive about its prospects for the rest of this year and for the longer term, the company said on Thursday.

"Our strong financial position enables us to pursue acquisition opportunities that match our strict strategic and financial criteria," the company said in a statement. Its pre-tax profit for the first six months of the year rose only one percent to 419 million pounds ($670.9 million) as the effects of sterling's strength were felt.
"Overall, we expect market conditions for the remainder of 1997 to be little different from those experienced in the first half," the company added.
"We are investing in new products and services to secure Reed Elsevier's continuing success and also in our programme to ensure full year 2000 compliance."
Reed said pre-tax profit rose 10 percent if measured at constant exchange rates.

The interim dividend for Reed shareholders was increased by seven percent to 4.4 pence while Elsevier shareholders will receive 0.29 guilders per share, an increase of 45 percent reflecting sterling's strength against the guilder.
The company has committed over 600 million pounds to more than 20 acquisitions since the start of the year.
Included in the committed spend is the 270 million pound acquisition of U.S. publisher Chilton Business Group which is expected to be completed shortly.
Chilton will be merged with the company's Cahners Publishing Company to form Reed Elsevier Business Information, which will have leading positions in important parts of the U.S. market.
